nodes.rationale: Structural anthropology is a named, academically recognized subfield of anthropology most strongly attributed to Claude Lévi-Strauss (reviewed), arising as a gap from the person-waves (decisions (67)/(71)); it is the direct object of the lévi-strauss→founded_or_formalized edge this batch needs.
nodes.uncertainty: QID Q860487 is a training-recall guess — QC must live-verify. The main substantive uncertainty is whether structural anthropology is better modeled as a methodological approach within cultural anthropology (concept or method node) rather than a peer subfield of field:anthropology; it is primarily a Lévi-Strauss-era phenomenon, and some would argue it dissolved into broader structuralism rather than persisting as an independent subfield.

edges.source_hint: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Claude Lévi-Strauss' (https://www.britannica.com/biography/Claude-Levi-Strauss); Wikipedia, 'Structural anthropology' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_anthropology); Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Claude Lévi-Strauss' or 'Structuralism'
edges.note: Reconciliation note: no existing edge edge:claude-levi-strauss-founded-or-formalized-structural-anthropology (or any variant) was found in data/edges.json at proposal time. The subfield:structural-anthropology target node is NEW in this batch (status generated), so this edge could not have been proposed previously. The lévi-strauss node was admitted in pivotal-influence-v1 with no founder edge because the target node was absent; this edge closes that gap. Both endpoints will be generated status until QC promotes the node. The founding attribution is essentially uncontested: structural anthropology is sometimes called 'Lévi-Strauss's structural anthropology' in secondary literature.
edges.rationale: Lévi-Strauss is the canonical and essentially sole founder/formalizer of structural anthropology; the field is defined by his application of structural linguistics methods to kinship, myth, and cultural analysis, starting with 'Elementary Structures of Kinship' (1949) and 'Structural Anthropology' (1958).
edges.uncertainty: Claim_anchors will be training-recall paraphrases — verbatim QC check required. The edge's validity inherits the node ambiguity: if QC reclassifies subfield:structural-anthropology as a method or concept node, the edge target changes. There is no serious rival candidate for this founding attribution, but the subfield's scope and persistence are contested.

edges.source_hint: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Roman Jakobson' (https://www.britannica.com/biography/Roman-Jakobson); Wikipedia, 'Roman Jakobson', §Contributions to linguistics; Wikipedia, 'Prague linguistic circle' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague_linguistic_circle)
edges.note: Co-founding with Nikolai Trubetzkoy (record-not-resolve): Jakobson and Trubetzkoy jointly developed structural/Prague School phonology in the 1920s–1930s; Trubetzkoy's 'Principles of Phonology' (Grundzüge der Phonologie, 1939) is typically cited as the foundational text, but Jakobson's parallel contributions (distinctive feature theory) are co-equal in the founding historiography. A future Trubetzkoy node edge would sit alongside this one. The Prague Linguistic Circle is the institutional founding context.
edges.rationale: Jakobson co-founded structural phonology (subfield:phonology, reviewed) with Trubetzkoy in the Prague Linguistic Circle; his distinctive-feature theory and phoneme concept are foundational contributions to the subfield.
edges.uncertainty: Claim_anchors will be training-recall paraphrases — verbatim QC check required. Trubetzkoy is the equal co-founder and is absent from this batch; QC should note the record-not-resolve co-founding and not read this edge as claiming Jakobson was the sole founder. Confidence 0.90 reflects the very strong founding attribution with the co-founding caveat.

edges.source_hint: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Claude Lévi-Strauss' (mentions Jakobson's role at the New School for Social Research); Wikipedia, 'Structural anthropology' §Influence of Roman Jakobson; Wikipedia, 'Roman Jakobson' §Influence on structuralism
edges.note: Endpoint selection decision: the order gives two options — Jakobson → subfield:structural-anthropology OR Jakobson → person:claude-levi-strauss. The person→person edge (E3) is chosen as the primary proposal because: (a) the historical claim is specifically about Jakobson's personal influence on Lévi-Strauss at the New School in New York in the early 1940s, not a diffuse field-level influence; (b) the data already carries edge:ferdinand-de-saussure-influenced-claude-levi-strauss (reviewed, note explicitly mentions 'transmission substantially mediated by Roman Jakobson'), making Jakobson→Lévi-Strauss the natural completion of that mediation chain; (c) person→person is a cleaner historical record-not-resolve pattern. A separate Jakobson→subfield:structural-anthropology edge could be added but would be redundant given E1 (lévi-strauss founded structural-anthropology) and E3 (jakobson influenced lévi-strauss). Confidence 0.95 — the Jakobson→Lévi-Strauss influence at the New School is extensively documented.
edges.rationale: Jakobson directly influenced Lévi-Strauss during their overlapping time at the New School for Social Research in New York in the early 1940s; Lévi-Strauss has acknowledged that Jakobson's structural phonology method was the model for his structural analysis of kinship and myth.
edges.uncertainty: Claim_anchors will be training-recall paraphrases — verbatim QC check required. The directness of influence is very well-attested in this case (unlike the Saussure→Lévi-Strauss edge which flagged the mediation question); the uncertainty is low but QC should confirm the specific claim about the New School encounter in at least two independent sources.

edges.source_hint: Wikipedia, 'Roman Jakobson', §Communication model; SEP entry on structuralism or semiotics if it covers Jakobson's role; Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'semiotics'
edges.note: Optional edge per the order ('if you find it well-grounded'). Rationale for including: Jakobson's communication model (addresser/message/addressee + context/contact/code, 1960 'Closing Statement: Linguistics and Poetics') is a canonical semiotic framework widely cited in semiotics literature; his distinctive-feature theory contributed to the sign-system analysis central to semiotics; and his role in transmitting Saussure's structural framework (via Lévi-Strauss and others) means his influence on semiotics is doubly mediated. However: this is a field-level influence, less direct than E3; semiotics had its own independent foundations (Peirce, Saussure); Jakobson's primary identity is as a linguist/phonologist, not a semiotician. Confidence 0.78 reflects genuine but secondary influence.
edges.rationale: Jakobson's communication model and his structural linguistics work are acknowledged influences on semiotics as a field; his 1960 'Linguistics and Poetics' communication model is a standard reference in semiotic curricula.
edges.uncertainty: The Jakobson→semiotics influence is real but diffuse — QC may judge the evidence insufficient for a 'influenced' edge vs. a weaker 'adjacent_to'; the claim rests on whether the communication model constitutes a field-level influence on semiotics or merely an adjacent contribution. Claim_anchors will be training-recall paraphrases requiring verbatim QC check.
